Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this on. We are running a private deployment evaluation for Redwood inside our VPC and the security/compliance team wants a concrete ops checklist and runbook for the KMS/HSM integration. Key asks from our side: BYOK import process, key rotation windows and automation, offline key import (split-key escrow), network egress constraints for HSMs, agent/daemon design for local encryption of artifacts, audit logging export, and procedures for emergency key recovery.

Can you share a draft runbook or checklist we can review? Prefer a step-by-step ops view (pre-deploy, deploy, validation, rotation, incident recovery) plus a list of required network rules and evidence artifacts for SOC2. I attached our high-level questionnaire to give context.

Attachments: acme_kms_questionnaire.pdf (3 pages)

High-level plan (will expand in doc):
- Pre-deploy: zoning (management/control plane vs data plane), HSM placement (on-prem HSM vs customer-managed cloud HSM), firewall rules (restrict outbound to our key-operator endpoints by IP), and KMS agent installation steps.
- Key import: documented BYOK flow — offline import steps, split-key escrow, operator sign-off, KMS fingerprints.
- Rotation: recommend rolling 30/90/365-day cadence by key-class; automated rotation using our ops-agent with manual approval window for primary keys.
- Audit/logs: retention targets and exported evidence (signing events, wrapping/unwrapping ops).
- Recovery: documented emergency procedures, escrow retrieval process, and post-recovery replay validation.

Proposed call slots: Wed 2/25 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 2/26 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?

Quick notes after reviewing Olga's draft — keeping short bullets for the call:

- Network: HSMs MUST be isolated in a dedicated management subnet. No inbound from public internet; only our agent on app hosts should reach the KMS over an explicit mTLS channel.
- Key wrapping: use data-encryption keys (DEKs) per tenant and keep master-wrapping-keys (MWKs) in HSM. DEKs cached in memory with TTL; do NOT persist plaintext.
- Rotation windows: implement phased rotation: rotate DEKs weekly with zero-downtime cache TTL refresh; rotate MWKs quarterly with canary hosts before global rollout.
- Operator tooling: offline BYOK import should produce cryptographic receipts; implement automatic audit-event push to customer SIEM over TLS-only syslog.
- Secrets handling: secrets-agent encrypts local config with DEK, stores only encrypted blobs; agent reloads on SIGHUP.

I'll bring a short diagram to the call showing agent<>HSM flows and the cache TTL behavior.

- Dev

Olga, Dev — good notes. A few additional constraints from our compliance team after an initial read:

- FIPS 140-2 validated HSM required for MWKs. Any software-based KMS is insufficient for master key custody.
- No persistent outbound connections from HSMs to external services — imports must be via offline hardware-token carry-in or through a secure jump host in our management VLAN.
- Split-key escrow: we need at least a 3-of-5 quorum model for escrow operators and a chain-of-custody form for each import/export event.
- Evidence: we require signed import receipts and time-stamped key lineage logs for 2 years.

We attached a small spreadsheet that maps our requirements to evidence artifacts (acme_kms_requirements.xlsx). Can you confirm which items Redwood will provide and which will be our responsibility? Also, please include how the canary rotation would be validated (proof that tokens were re-encrypted and no downtime).

Thanks — happy to discuss on the call.

— Samir Patel

Samir — great context, thanks. Below is an agreed proposed runbook summary and owner map; I'll convert into the formal doc and share the Drive link + next steps after your sign-off.

Proposed runbook (summary):
1) Pre-deploy (owners: Acme infra + Redwood SE)
   - Validate management VLAN and dedicated HSM subnet; confirm jump-host ops workflow (owner: Acme)
   - Exchange operator PGP keys and bootstrap 3-of-5 escrow officer list (owner: Acme)
   - Provide preferred HSM model and FIPS evidence (owner: Acme)

2) BYOK import (owners: Redwood ops + Acme security)
   - Offline import steps: create MWK locally on HSM appliance, export split-wrapped fragments to escrow officers; collect signed import receipts (operator signatures & timestamps)
   - Redwood to provide import scripts, import-checksum generator, and verification checklist

3) Deployment & validation (owners: Redwood dev + Acme infra)
   - Install Redwood secrets-agent on app hosts; configure mTLS to HSM management endpoint; validate DEK wrap/unwrap across 3 canary hosts
   - Run automated validation: wrap/unwrap N=100 sample keys, verify audit event export to customer SIEM

4) Rotation & rollout (owners: Redwood dev + Acme security)
   - Canary rotation window: start with 1% hosts, validate re-encryption integrity, then expand 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m observation windows
   - MWK quarterly rotation: schedule with maintenance window and operator approval; maintain key lineage mapping

5) Emergency recovery (owners: Acme security + Redwood support)
   - Escrow retrieval steps and chain-of-custody validation; post-recovery integrity checks and forced re-encrypt of all DEKs

Validation artifacts we will provide:
- Signed import receipts (PDF)
- Audit event bundle (TLS-signed, time-stamped)
- Canary run report (logs + checksums)

Action items / next steps:
- Acme: confirm escrow officer list and preferred call slot (we suggest Thu 2/26 14:00 PT).
- Redwood: finalize the doc, produce import scripts and a pre-deploy checklist by Mon 3/2.
